# Set-ZbxUser

## SYNOPSIS

Changes a user.

## SYNTAX

```
Set-ZbxUser [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]> [[-Username] <string>] [-FirstName <string>] [-LastName <string>] [-CurrentPassword <SecureString>] [-Password <SecureString>] [-Url <string>] [-AutoLogin <bool>] [-AutoLogout <string>] [-Language <string>] [-Refresh <string>] [-Theme <string>] [-RowsPerPage <int>] [-Timezone <string>] [-RoleId <ulong>] [-UserGroup <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUserGroup>[]>] [-Media <ZabbixUserUpdateMediaRequest[]>] [-DefaultMaintenancePeriod <string>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-PassThru] [-PipedRecord <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A user is an account that logs in to the frontend or the API, with its role, its user groups and the media it is notified on. The Set-ZbxUser cmdlet changes the users given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with user.update; a field whose parameter is not given keeps its value. Every user the pipeline brings is changed in one call when the pipeline ends, and -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name. The command writes nothing unless -PassThru is given, which reads the changed users back and writes them; -WhatIf shows what would change.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Change a user's language and time zone

```powershell
Set-ZbxUser -InputObject 'jdoe' -Language 'de_DE' -Timezone 'Europe/Berlin' -PassThru | Select-Object Username, Language, Timezone
```

-InputObject (position 0) takes the user's name, id or object; a parameter not given keeps its value.

### Example 2: Move a user to other user groups

```powershell
Set-ZbxUser -InputObject 'jdoe' -UserGroup 'Operators' -WhatIf
```

-UserGroup replaces the user's groups; give every group the user should stay in.

### Example 3: Set a new password

```powershell
Set-ZbxUser -InputObject 'jdoe' -Password (ConvertTo-SecureString 'N3w-passw0rd-for-jdoe!' -AsPlainText -Force)
```

The password is a SecureString, never a plain string.
